newsitem.title: FRANCE: TOTAL CONFIDENT OF RENEWING IRAQ OIL DEAL.
newsitem.headline: TOTAL CONFIDENT OF RENEWING IRAQ OIL DEAL.

text.p: French oil group Total SA said it was confident of renewing its 30,000 bpd oil deal with Iraq.
"For us it is business as usual with (Iraq's state oil company) SOMO. We are confident of signing a new deal of the same size as our current deal," a spokesman said.
Earlier, Elf-Aquitaine said it expected to renew its 20,000 bpd deal while Royal Dutch/Shell and British Petroleum said they had indications their contracts would not be renewed.

Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) is hosting a meeting with oil companies in Baghdad next week to finalise the deals for the second phase of the oil-for-aid deal under United States auspices.
"We have been invited to come to Baghdad for talks and we expect to sign a contract for an amount close to the 20,000 bpd we have now," said a spokesman for Elf.
"The Iraqi's have sent a price list to the U.N. and that should normally be approved in the coming days," he added.
Iraq's oil minister Amir Mohammed Rasheed said on Wednesday he expected the country to resume crude exports between August 15 and 20.
Portugal's Petrogal expects to lift around 11,000 bpd from Kirkuk.
BP has a contract for 10,000 bpd while Shell had an allocation of 30,000 bpd.
Iraq's second phase of sales had been delayed for two months to allow modifications to aid distribution plans.
Earlier this month, Iraq resumed buying of grain with a purchase of at least 50,000 tonnes of wheat from the U.S.
Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the U.N. was set up to alleviate the impact on civilians of sanctions imposed on the country after its troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
The second phase allows Iraq to export $2.4 billion of oil over 180 days originally due to have started on June 8.
During the first 180 day period from last December, Iraq sold some 700,000 bpd and bought an estimated 1.3 million tonnes in wheat.
